'''Thakurartha Devadithya Guardiyawasam Lindamulage Nalin Kumar de Silva ''' ([[Sinhala language|Sinhala]]: නලින් ද සිල්වා; 20 October 1944 – 1 May 2024) was a [[Sri Lanka]]n philosopher,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.vidusara.com/2011/07/27/readers1.html |title=Readers1 |access-date=20 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116222228/http://www.vidusara.com/2011/07/27/readers1.html |archive-date=16 January 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=damith |date=2024-05-04 |title=Dr. Nalin de Silva's funeral in California today |url=https://www.sundayobserver.lk/2024/05/05/news/22573/dr-nalin-de-silvas-funeral-in-california-today/ |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=Sunday Observer |language=en-US}}</ref> polymath and a political analyst. He was the former Sri Lankan ambassador in [[Myanmar]].<ref>https://divaina.com/sunday/index.php/visheshanga1/14020-2020-05-09-13-00-69 {{dead link|date=August 2021}}</ref> He was a professor in the department of mathematics, a member of University Grant Commission and the dean of the faculty of science at the [[University of Kelaniya]], Sri Lanka.

De Silva openly stated that the so-called 'objective scientific method' was a lie.<ref>{{cite web|last=De Silva|first=Nalin|title=The importance of learning English/ Mathematics – V|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=20138|publisher=The Island|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022094726/http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=20138|archive-date=22 October 2012|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Chemical Arsenic and other Arsenics|url=http://epaper.divaina.com/index.php?option=com_flippingbook&view=book&id=245&page=1|newspaper=The Sunday Divaina|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328162427/http://epaper.divaina.com/index.php?option=com_flippingbook&view=book&id=245&page=1|archive-date=28 March 2012|url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2011 he stated that information regarding the presence of [[arsenic]] in water claiming that the cause of Rajarata chronic kidney disease had been given to him by the god [[Maitreya|Natha]].<ref name="auto1">{{cite news|title=Devivaru, Arsenic and Science|url=http://www.srilankaguardian.org/2011/06/devivaru-arsenic-and-science.html|newspaper=Sri Lanka Guardian|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724053215/http://www.srilankaguardian.org/2011/06/devivaru-arsenic-and-science.html|archive-date=24 July 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> The Sri Lanka Association for the Advancement of Science, an organisation in which De Silva claimed lifelong membership, has said that they consider it "extremely unfortunate that the Dean of a Science Faculty should make it his publicly stated aim to run down science and bring it into disrepute."<ref name="auto3">{{cite web|last=SLAAS|title=SLAAS refutes Arsenic claims|url=http://www.dailynews.lk/2011/07/08/news41.asp|publisher=The Daily News|access-date=7 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824061356/http://www.dailynews.lk/2011/07/08/news41.asp|archive-date=24 August 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> However the presence of arsenic was verified in water and vegetation, and the source was found to be agrochemical fertilizers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Charita|first=Wijeratne|title=Arsenic or not pesticides are deadly|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=29782|publisher=The Island|accessdate=9 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110712143326/http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=29782|archive-date=12 July 2011|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Ockersz|first=Lynne|title=Arsenic in water placing 'whole nation at risk' says scientis|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=20846|publisher=The Island|accessdate=16 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819103107/http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=20846|archive-date=19 August 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Nalin de Silva was born on 20 October 1944 in Kovilagodella, [[Panadura]], Sri Lanka. His father was Daniel De Silva, a principal, and his mother was Jayline Perera, a school teacher. De Silva was the eldest of eight siblings. He had primary education at Bauddhaloka Maha Vidyalaya, [[Thurstan College]] Colombo and secondary education at [[Royal College Colombo]].  He captained the Sinhala Debating team at Royal College and won the Weerasooriya medal for oratory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kln.ac.lk/science/maths/page/staff/Nalinda.html |title=Prof. L.N.K.De Silva |access-date=5 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928033006/http://www.kln.ac.lk/science/maths/page/staff/Nalinda.html |archive-date=28 September 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref>
He entered the [[University of Ceylon]] in 1963 and graduated in mathematics in 1967. De Silva entered [[University of Sussex]] in January 1969, where he obtained his doctorate in theoretical physics –[[cosmology]] – in 1970.

He was married and had two sons and one daughter.{{Citation needed|date=May 2024}}

== Academic work ==
[[File:Nalin de Silva.jpg|left|upright|thumb|273px|Professor Nalin de Silva in 2014.]]

=== Constructive relativism ===
Nalin de Silva was formally a member of the Marxist [[Trotskyist]] [[Lanka Sama Samaja Party]] and the [[Nava Sama Samaja Party]], and as a Marxist studying both disciplines he intensively began to question the foundations of both [[Marxism]] and science. As a result, in 1986, he wrote ''Mage Lokaya'' (My World), criticising the basis of the established western system of knowledge, and its propagation, which he refers as "domination throughout the world". He explained in this book that mind independent reality is impossible and knowledge is not found but constructed.

This has further evolved into a study of [[epistemology]] and [[ontology]], and in the process he has introduced and developed the concept of "constructive relativism"<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kalaya.org/npe051127.html |title=Constructive Relativism |access-date=15 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112080215/http://www.kalaya.org/npe051127.html |archive-date=12 January 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> as the basis on which knowledge is constructed relative to the sense organs, culture and the mind completely based on [[Avidyā (Buddhism)|Avidya]]. Though he was identified as a representative of "Jathika Chinthanaya" an idea proposed by [[Gunadasa Amarasekara]] based on national thought concept of [[Erich Fromm]], Nalin de Silva's concept Chinthanaya is a different epistemological concept.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www1.kalaya.org/2013/05/blog-post_1036.html |title=මාක්ස්වාදය හා දැනුම් ගස් |access-date=1 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501225538/http://www1.kalaya.org/2013/05/blog-post_1036.html |archive-date=1 May 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Vidyalankara interpretation ===
Vidyalankara interpretation was presented based on the theoretical and experimental work conducted by Dr. Nalin de Silva and his student Suraj Chandana at University of Kelaniya (Vidyalankara) in which Dr. de Silva rejects the wave nature of particles. According to him what gives rise to a bright and dark fringe pattern in the Young's double slit experiment is not the so called wave nature but the particle nature itself though not necessarily those of ordinary classical particles. Dr. de Silva theorises that each particle that hit the screen on a double slit experiment appears at both the slits simultaneously prior to reaching the screen. According to Janaka Wansapura, Ph.D. this is a paradigm shift in the knowledge of quantum nature.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.4712v1.pdf Quantum Physics in a different ontology - Nalin de Silva]</ref><ref>[https://www.lankaweb.com/news/items/2012/02/02/wave-particle-duality-of-nature-challenged-at-kelaniya-university/ Wave-particle duality of nature challenged at Kelaniya University - Janaka Wansapura]</ref>

=== Accelerating and decelerating Universe ===
Dr. Nalin de Silva has given a model for the universe with both acceleration and deceleration.<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/1778525_A_Universe_with_both_acceleration_and_deceleration A Universe with both acceleration and deceleration - Nalin de Silva]</ref>

=== Arsenic controversy ===
The Rajarata chronic kidney disease (RCKD) has been an ailment prevalent in the [[North Central Province, Sri Lanka|North Central Province of Sri Lanka]] for several decades. In 2010 a team of scientists headed by Priyani Paranagama, head of the chemistry department at Kelaniya University, conducted a study to find the cause of the disease. The team was advised by Nalin de Silva, dean of the faculty of science, Kelaniya University.<ref>{{cite news|title=Arsenic is attributed to kidney ailment in North Central Province|url=http://www.itnnews.lk/?p=26155|newspaper=ITN News|access-date=20 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110625171000/http://www.itnnews.lk/?p=26155|archive-date=25 June 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> The team presented their findings in June 2011. They stated that they had found high concentrations of [[arsenic]] in drinking water, vegetation, rice and other samples in the region.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fernando|first=Manjula|title=Key to mystery killer disease found|url=https://archives.sundayobserver.lk/2011/06/12/fea11.asp|newspaper=The Sunday Observer|access-date=7 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110822103714/http://www.sundayobserver.lk/2011/06/12/fea11.asp|archive-date=22 August 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> The team, however, refused to release their data to the public, raising questions about their methodology.<ref name="auto2">{{cite news|title=Furore over arsenic shakes agri sector|url=http://www.nation.lk/2011/06/19/newsfe10.htm|newspaper=The Nation|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726072915/http://www.nation.lk/2011/06/19/newsfe10.htm|archive-date=26 July 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> Their finding were followed by allegations that the arsenic was being introduced to the system through foreign pesticides and fertilizers.<ref>{{cite news|title=High levels of arsenic in pesticides|url=http://print.dailymirror.lk/opinion1/46604.html|newspaper=The Daily Mirror|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807005611/http://print.dailymirror.lk/opinion1/46604.html|archive-date=7 August 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As this statement caused a huge uproar in the agricultural sector in Sri Lanka, the Industrial Technology Institute stated that they had used [[Atomic absorption spectroscopy|Hydride Generation Atomic Absorption Spectrometry]] on rice samples which showed no high levels of arsenic.<ref>{{cite news|title=No Arsenic found in Sri Lankan Local Rice – ITI|url=http://news.lk/home/18346-no-arsenic-found-in-sri-lankan-local-rice-iti|newspaper=Government Information Department – Sri Lanka|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110704005124/http://www.news.lk/home/18346-no-arsenic-found-in-sri-lankan-local-rice-iti|archive-date=4 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> The ITI study also found that in samples of 28 different pesticides only 3 showed any signs of arsenic, and even then not in the concentrations that De Silva's team alleged.<ref name="auto2"/> The Kelaniya University team stated that they had used new methods to locate the Arsenic in the samples they collected but did not feel a need to submit their findings for peer-review.<ref>{{cite web|last=SLAAS Statement|title=SLAAS refutes Arsenic claims|url=http://www.dailynews.lk/2011/07/08/news41.asp|publisher=The Daily News|access-date=7 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824061356/http://www.dailynews.lk/2011/07/08/news41.asp|archive-date=24 August 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> De Silva stated that they did not publish their results in a "so-called peer reviewed journal due to our concern regarding the authorship of the paper as the original idea was given by 'samyak drshtika devivaru'  also known as [[Deva (Buddhism)|Devas]].<ref>{{cite news|last=De Silva|first=Nalin|title=Statement by SLAAS on Arsenic studies|url=http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=29428|newspaper=The Island|access-date=7 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022093913/http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=29428|archive-date=22 October 2012|url-status=live}}</ref>

When the authenticity of the findings made by the University of Kelaniya team were questioned by other scientists, De Silva stated that the god "Natha" had first told them about the arsenic through a mystic.
<blockquote>The merit (pina) in this regard should go to the "samyak drshtika devivaru" who first told that Arsenic is present in Rajarata drinking water and later revealed to us that Arsenic which is not found naturally in Sri Lanka has found its way to the wells and the wewas in Rajarata through Agrochemicals.<ref name="auto1"/> </blockquote>

<blockquote>It's simply like this. We can see professors. Professors cannot see Arsenic. We cannot see gods. Gods can see Arsenic. I like this because there is certain symmetry in it... I know very well that the so-called objective scientific method is a lie.<ref>{{cite news|last=De Silva|first=Nalin|title=Chemical Arsenic and other Arsenics|url=http://epaper.divaina.com/index.php?option=com_flippingbook&view=book&id=245&page=1|newspaper=The Sunday Divaina|date=15 May 2011|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328162427/http://epaper.divaina.com/index.php?option=com_flippingbook&view=book&id=245&page=1|archive-date=28 March 2012|url-status=live}}</ref></blockquote>

Paranagama too has stood by De Silva and defended their methods. She said that they had first been told of the arsenic by the wife of "a university lecturer who had developed her mental faculties to communicate with a higher being", but then used scientific methods to deduce it.<ref>{{cite news|last=Weerasekera|first=Mangala|title=Scientists say Gods and tests helped detect arsenic in agrochemicals|url=http://sundaytimes.lk/110703/News/nws_12.html|newspaper=The Sunday Times|access-date=7 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711153159/http://www.sundaytimes.lk/110703/News/nws_12.html|archive-date=11 July 2011|url-status=live}}</ref>

The Sri Lanka Association for the Advancement of Science released a statement in July 2011 questioning the validity of the findings and the process and individuals involved in the study. Their statement laid the blame for the scandal firmly on Prof Nalin De Silva, and they called for other scientists and researchers in the group to distance themselves from De Silva to have their work taken seriously {{citation needed|date=March 2015}}.

<blockquote>There is another serious issue which casts grave doubts on the credibility of the claims made by the Kelaniya group. The press has publicly identified as the leader of this group an individual, who despite holding a responsible position, professes a disdain for 'Western' science. He has publicly claimed supernatural revelations ('samyak drushtika devivaru') as the source of his group's information and even methods. While recognising that many scientists are deeply religious, the SLAAS wishes to state categorically that superstition and the supernatural have no place in science, and that scientific results inspired by such sources are highly suspect because of a probable bias on the part of the investigator.

We also note that other researchers in the group have yet to distance themselves from the eccentric statements of their leader, and they need to do this if they wish to be taken seriously as scientists.<ref name="auto3"/></blockquote>

=== Western cultural dominance ===
De Silva was also a vocal opponent of what he calls western cultural dominance which he claimed is in its final phase.
<blockquote>The western Christian modernity (WCM) is in the last phase of its hegemony and is acting like an insane person. It has no respect for the sovereignty of the other countries as has been exemplified from invasions, killings and supporting so called rebel groups in the countries in Asia and Africa. The USA that became the leader of WCM after the so called second world war is trying desperately to hold to the hegemony of WCM. After more than five hundred years of world domination WCM will have to leave the planet without making the people suffer more and more.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|last=De Silva|first=Nalin|title=Get ready for a humanitarian attack|url=http://www1.kalaya.org/2011/05/get-ready-for-humanitarian-attack.html|publisher=Kalaya|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110820082302/http://www1.kalaya.org/2011/05/get-ready-for-humanitarian-attack.html|archive-date=20 August 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> </blockquote>

De Silva also referred to linguist and philosopher [[Noam Chomsky]] as a puppet of the Western Christian Modernity.
<blockquote>The west also maintains people such as Chomsky who is not known to the average American in order to show to the world that there is freedom for the intellectuals to champion their views heard more by the rest of the world than by the Americans themselves.<ref name="auto"/></blockquote>

=== Philosophy of science ===
De Silva, who was influenced by [[Paul Feyerabend]], rejected the existence of scientific method and proposed proliferation of sciences on various chinthanayas.<ref>Vidya Kathandara (Science Stories) Vidya Kathandara (Stories of Science) https://www.sarasavi.lk/Book/Vidya-Kathandara-9559170600 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502064110/https://www.sarasavi.lk/Book/Vidya-Kathandara-9559170600 |date=2 May 2018 }}</ref>

De Silva proposed theories are stories constructed by [[abductive reasoning]] to explain phenomena.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sarasavi.lk/Book/Vidya-Kathandara-9559170600 |title=Vidya Kathandara |access-date=1 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502064110/https://www.sarasavi.lk/Book/Vidya-Kathandara-9559170600 |archive-date=2 May 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref>

De Silva refused ideas that science is truth or science is advancing towards the truth.<ref>MLA	
De Silva, Nalin. Mage lokaya. 1992.</ref>

=== Sacking from University of Colombo ===
De Silva was sacked from the University of Colombo for engaging in unlawful political activity within the campus. In subsequent letters he has described the event.
<blockquote>When I was in the University of Colombo, not the best place to fight the cultural pentagon, I was asked by the then Vice Chancellor [[G. L. Peiris]] why I was teaching Jathika Chinthanaya to a captive audience. The audience was not that captive and had the backing of the Vice Chancellor and some members of the senior staff, and of course the cultural pentagon. Nothing happened to the captive audience but soon I found that I was out of the University system.<ref>{{cite web|last=De Silva|first=Pentagon|url=http://www.island.lk/2008/02/13/midweek2.html|publisher=The Island|title=Cultural Pentagon by Nalin de Silva|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100927223153/http://www.island.lk/2008/02/13/midweek2.html|archive-date=27 September 2010|url-status=live}}</ref> </blockquote>

=== Veemansaka Parshadaya ===
In 2008 the Veemansaka Parshadaya, a student organisation where De Silva is the treasurer and mentor started a campaign to ban western clothing in Kelaniya University.<ref>{{cite web|last=De Silva|first=Nalin|title=Cultural Pentagon|url=http://www.island.lk/2008/02/13/midweek2.html|publisher=The Island|access-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100927223153/http://www.island.lk/2008/02/13/midweek2.html|archive-date=27 September 2010|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Associations ==
Nalin de Silva was a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lindamulage Nalin de Silva. |url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/5790/ |website=Iau.org}}</ref>

== Death ==
De Silva died on 1 May 2024 in Fremont, California, at the age of 79.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Derana |first1=Ada |title=Philosopher & intellectual Professor Nalin de Silva passes away at the age of 79 years |url=https://twitter.com/adaderana/status/1786035391751200972}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Nalin Silva's funeral in California tomorrow |date=4 May 2024 |url=https://english.theleader.lk/news/8563-nalin-silva-s-funeral-in-california-tomorrow |access-date=5 May 2024 |archive-date=5 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240505020749/https://english.theleader.lk/news/8563-nalin-silva-s-funeral-in-california-tomorrow |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":0" />
